# Tobit Chapter 8 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 8 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_008_page_001.jpg

---

**8:1** When they had finished eating, they brought Tobias in to her.

**8:2** As he went in, he remembered the words of Raphael. He took the incense ashes and laid upon them the heart and liver of the fish, and made smoke with them.

**8:3** The demon smelled it and fled to the upper parts of Egypt, and Raphael went and bound him there, shackled forever.

**8:4** When they were shut in together, Tobias rose from the bed and said, "Rise, my sister, and let us pray that the Lord will have mercy upon us."

**8:5** Tobias began and said: "Blessed are you, O God of our fathers, and blessed is your name throughout all the ages of ages. Let the heavens bless you, and all your creation, throughout all the ages.

**8:6** You made Adam and gave him Eve his wife as helper and support; from both of them came the seed of all mankind. You yourself said, 'It is not good for the man to be alone; let us make for him a helper like himself.'

**8:7** And now, O Lord, it is not out of lust that I take this my sister, but in truth. Command that mercy be shown to me and to her, and that we may come to old age together."

**8:8** They both said together, "Amen, amen."

**8:9** They slept through the night. Raguel rose and went out and dug a grave,

**8:10** saying, "Perhaps he will die as well." And Raguel went back into his house

**8:11** and said to his wife Edna, "Send one of the maidservants to look and see whether he is alive; and if he is not, we will bury him before anyone finds out."

**8:12** The maidservant opened the door and went in and found them both asleep.

**8:13** She came out and told them that he was alive.

**8:14** Then Raguel blessed God, saying: "Blessed are you, O God, with every pure and holy blessing. Let your holy ones bless you, and all your creatures and all your angels and all your chosen ones, forever.

**8:15** Blessed are you, because you have made me glad, and what I feared has not come to pass; rather, you have dealt with us according to your great mercy.

**8:16** Blessed are you, because you have had mercy on these two only children. Show them mercy, O Master; grant them health in life, joy, mercy, and gladness.

**8:17** Grant them, O Lord, long life in gladness."

**8:18** Then he commanded his servants to fill in the grave before daylight.

**8:19** He told his wife to bake many loaves of bread, and he himself went to the herd and brought two oxen and four rams and commanded them to be prepared. And they began their preparations.

**8:20** He called Tobias and swore to him, saying, "You shall not leave here for fourteen days,

**8:21** but shall stay here eating and drinking with me, and shall gladden the heart of my daughter who has been deeply afflicted. Take half of all that I possess and return in peace to your father; the other half will be yours when my wife and I have died. Take heart, my child. I am your father, and Edna is your mother, and we belong to you and your sister, now and forever. Take heart, child."

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Chapter 8 required deliberation on four primary questions: (1) how to render the exorcism scene without over-dramatizing or flattening it; (2) the correct force of the prayer's moral contrast in verse 7; (3) the tone of Raguel's grave-digging sequence; and (4) the inheritance language in verse 21.

On verse 7's central contrast: all three agents agree that ep' porneia carries a pejorative force ("lust" rather than "desire"). SOPHIA adopts LOGOS/EMET's "out of lust" over PNEUMA's "because of physical desire" as more concise and resonant. "In truth" (ep' aletheias) is retained from EMET/LOGOS; PNEUMA's "with a true heart" is evocative but interpretive.

On the exorcism (vv. 2-3): LOGOS's spare rendering is adopted. PNEUMA's "fled all the way to the far reaches" is lively but adds to the text; EMET's "upper-parts" hyphenation is too literal for SOPHIA's register.

On Raguel's grave (v. 9): LOGOS's minimal treatment — "rose and went out and dug a grave" — is preferred. The scene needs no commentary.

On verse 21: LOGOS's "belong to you" for the family-adoption language is adopted over EMET's more archaic phrasing and PNEUMA's expansive "you are our son now."

---
## Disagreement Log

| Verse | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | SOPHIA Resolution |
|-------|------|-------|--------|-------------------|
| 8:2 | "ashes-of the incense" | "ashes of the incense" | "incense ashes" | "incense ashes" — natural and clear |
| 8:3 | "upper-parts-of Egypt" | "upper parts of Egypt" | "far reaches of Egypt" | "upper parts of Egypt" — literal geography preserved |
| 8:4 | "Rise, sister" | "Rise up, my sister" | "Come, my sister" | "Rise, my sister" — retains the direct call without adding "up" |
| 8:7 | "not on-account-of lust… but on-account-of truth" | "not out of lust… but in truth" | "not because of physical desire… honestly, with a true heart" | "not out of lust… but in truth" — LOGOS rendering adopted |
| 8:9 | "slept for the night" / "rose and went and dug" | "slept through the night" / "rose and went out and dug" | "they slept. Meanwhile…" | "slept through the night" / "rose and went out and dug" |
| 8:10 | "Perhaps he also will die" | "Perhaps he will die as well" | "What if this one dies too?" | "Perhaps he will die as well" — formal without being archaic |
| 8:11 | "that no-one may know [about it]" | "before anyone finds out" | "before anyone finds out" | "before anyone finds out" — LOGOS/PNEUMA agreement adopted |
| 8:14 | "let your holy ones bless you, and all your creatures, and all your angels, and your chosen-ones" | "Let your holy ones bless you, and all your creatures, and all your angels, and all your chosen ones" | "May your holy ones praise you, and all your creatures and angels and chosen people" | LOGOS rendering; "bless" over "praise" for doxological consistency |
| 8:16 | "two only-children" | "two only children" | "two young people who are all each other had" | "two only children" — preserves the Greek monogeneis texture |
| 8:19 | "two oxen and four rams" | "two oxen and four rams" | "two bulls and four rams" | "two oxen and four rams" — EMET/LOGOS agreement; "oxen" fits the sacrificial/feast register |
| 8:21 | "half-of what I possess" | "half of all that I possess" | "half of everything I own" | "half of all that I possess" — LOGOS natural formality |
| 8:21 | "we are yours and your sister's" | "we belong to you and to your sister" | "you are our son now… this is your home" | "we belong to you and your sister" — LOGOS; PNEUMA's expansion not supported by text |
